req.title: Return DELETE request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that DELETE /delete returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, and origin. Tests are designed to: (1) verify the positive path with a plain DELETE request and assert all required keys exist with exact types/values; (2) verify a negative path by sending a wrong HTTP method (GET to /delete) and asserting 405; (3) verify boundary behavior with query-string args and JSON body in the DELETE request; (4) verify that the 'args' field reflects query parameters exactly; (5) verify that the 'json' field is populated when Content-Type is application/json. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximize mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
No special headers or body required
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send DELETE request to /delete with no body or query params
expected: JSON body contains exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010: DELETE /delete -> HTTP 200 with JSON body reflecting DELETE payload
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.content_type
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    required_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == required_keys
    assert body['args'] == {}
    assert body['form'] == {}
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['files'] == {}
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert isinstance(body['url'], str)
    assert 'delete' in body['url']

test_delete_plain_returns_200_and_all_required_keys()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_with_query_args_reflected_in_args_field():
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar&baz=qux')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar', 'baz': 'qux'}
    assert 'foo=bar' in body['url'] or 'baz=qux' in body['url']
    assert body['form'] == {}
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert body['files'] == {}

test_delete_with_query_args_reflected_in_args_field()

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_delete_response_keys_are_exactly_the_required_set():
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    actual_keys = set(body.keys())
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    missing = expected_keys - actual_keys
    assert missing == set(), f'Missing keys: {missing}'
    extra = actual_keys - expected_keys
    assert extra == set(), f'Unexpected extra keys: {extra}'

test_delete_response_keys_are_exactly_the_required_set()
